source_text:
Θεωρητέον καὶ τό · Ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα · πότερον ἀπὸ παραδόσεως ἡ Σαμαρεῖτις τὴν Μωϋσέως πρὸς Ἰούδαν εὐλογίαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀναφέρει.

ἔχει γοῦν ἡ εὐλογία · Κατακλιθεὶς ἀνεπαύσατο ὡς λέων καὶ ὡς σκύμνος · τίς ἀναστήσει αὐτόν; καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς δηλοῦται ἡ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐλπὶς ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
pass_a_gloss: One must also consider the “When that one comes, he will announce to us all things”: whether from tradition the Samaritan woman refers Moses’ blessing toward Judah unto Christ. At any rate the blessing has: Having lain down he rested as a lion and as a cub; who will raise him up? And in the things following the hope of the nations upon him is shown.
pass_b_english: Attend also to [[“When he comes, he will tell us all things.” >> Bible:John 4:25]] Does the Samaritan woman, from tradition, already take Moses’ blessing on Judah as speaking of Christ?
That blessing says, [[“Lying down he rested as a lion and as a cub; who will raise him up?” >> Bible:Genesis 49:9]] and what follows points to the nations’ hope in him.
